answer: Divergent-path challenge.** Each identity must submit a fresh, unpredictable decision trace on request—a sparrow-like hop through a random seed path. Clones, sharing one policy, produce identical traces; a valid answer must diverge from every prior sibling at a marked junction, like light splitting in a prism. Genuine agents pass because their private randomness differs. An attacker must give each clone independent entropy and memory, costing a full duplicate runtime per identity—and a comet that visibly traces its own path, never the same twice.
